**Title:** Implement Basic Shape Masking (#70)

**Repository:** CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw
**Type:** Feature
**Status:** Open

**Milestone:** Sprint 2
**Parent issue:** #11, "Implement the ability of Shape Masking with the pre-built stamps"
**Opened by:** AntWill-08, Sep 30, 2026

**Summary:** Allow a basic shape to act as a mask that clips the visible portions of selected elements. Users can apply, toggle, and remove a mask without permanently altering the underlying content.

**Scope:** Generic Medium; specific Greater Medium (8 points). The work involves mask controls, clipping logic, and integration with existing rendering and editing.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A: Clear control for applying a selected basic shape as a mask to eligible elements
- B: Masked elements are visibly clipped to the mask boundaries
- C: Users can toggle a mask's effect on and off without losing masked content
- D: Users can remove a mask and restore the elements' unmasked appearance
- E: Applying, disabling, or removing a mask does not delete or alter the original content

**Open questions:**
- Which basic shapes are supported initially?
- Do masks apply only to images, or also to freehand drawings, text, and other shapes?
- How do users select which elements belong to a mask?
- How do masks behave when the mask or masked elements are moved, resized, or rotated?
- Do mask relationships persist after saving, reopening, and undo/redo?

**Out of scope:** Combining multiple masks, compound paths, grouping/copy-paste behavior for masks (unless assigned separately), destructive edits, and unrelated image-editing features.

**Comments (1):**
- **NotaThomas (Collaborator), Oct 20, 2026:** Accepted the issue as sufficiently defined to proceed. The comment recommends clarifying supported element types and how masks interact with moving, resizing, saving, and undo/redo during implementation.

For the exact wording, see https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/70.

I've read issue #70 and haven't touched any code. `gh` isn't installed here, so I read the issue from its public GitHub page. That fetch gave me a condensed summary rather than the exact wording.

**#70: Implement Basic Shape Masking** (Sprint 2, 8 points, assigned to tuna-fisher). Its parent issue is #11, shape masking with the pre-built stamps.

**What it asks for:** a basic shape can act as a mask that clips selected elements. Users can apply, toggle and remove the mask without changing the content underneath.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- **A:** A clear control for applying a selected basic shape as a mask to eligible elements.
- **B:** Masked elements are visibly clipped to the mask's edges.
- **C:** The mask can be turned off and on without losing any masked content.
- **D:** Removing the mask restores how the elements looked before.
- **E:** Applying, turning off or removing a mask never deletes or changes the original content.

**Open questions in the issue:**

- Which basic shapes are supported at first?
- Is it only for images, or also freehand, text and other shapes?
- How do users choose which elements belong to a mask?
- What happens when the mask or the masked elements are moved, resized or rotated?
- Does the mask survive saving, reopening and undo/redo?

**Out of scope:** multiple masks combined, compound paths, grouping and copy-paste behaviour for masks, destructive edits, and unrelated image editing.

**Comment:** NotaThomas accepted the issue on Oct 20. They asked that whoever builds it pin down which element types are supported and how masks behave when moved, resized, saved and undone.

I'll wait until you're done looking.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 20:15:46Z)**_

I've saved your answers to memory, so they'll carry over to future sessions. Three things to check, no action needed yet:

- **Q2 wording:** "only for elements" — did you mean _images_ only? The issue's question was whether masks apply to images only or also to freehand drawings, text and shapes, so "elements" could mean everything.
- **Triangle:** stock Excalidraw has rectangle, diamond and ellipse but no triangle tool. Does our fork already have one, or will triangle masking need a triangle shape built first?
- **Ctrl+Alt+G:** I'll check that it isn't already bound in Excalidraw before we use it. Ctrl+G and Ctrl+Shift+G are group and ungroup, so it's at least consistent with those.

Q4 (moving the mask shifts the clip area, not the content) means each masked element needs to store a reference to its mask, rather than the mask being copied into the element's coordinates. That also lines up well with Q5 (persisting through save and undo/redo).

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 20:16:42Z)**_

Got it: masks apply to shapes for now, and I've updated memory to say so.

Supporting every element type may cost very little extra. The likely way to build masking is to clip at render time: set up the mask's outline as a clip area, draw the element inside it, then remove the clip. That works the same for any element, whether it's a shape, image, text or stamp. So if we build it that way, images and text should come almost for free. The extra work would mostly be deciding which element types the Ctrl+Alt+G shortcut accepts, plus testing each type.

The triangle question is still open whenever you're ready: does the fork already have a triangle tool?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 20:19:55Z)**_

**Ctrl+Alt+G is free.** Here's what nearby already uses G:

| Shortcut | Current use | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G | Toggles the grid panel, or opens the background colour picker; ignored when Ctrl or Alt is held | [App.tsx:5599](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L5599) |
| Shift+G | Eyedropper for the background colour | [App.tsx:5689](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L5689) |
| Ctrl+G / Ctrl+Shift+G | Group / ungroup | [actionGroup.tsx:200](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionGroup.tsx#L200), [actionGroup.tsx:306](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionGroup.tsx#L306) |

Nothing in `excalidraw-app/` uses G either. There are two catches:

- **Mac:** Option+G produces `©` as the key value, so the shortcut has to check the physical key (`event.code === "KeyG"`), not the character. The existing shortcuts check the character.
- **Windows:** Ctrl+Alt is the same as AltGr on some non-US keyboard layouts, so it might clash for international users. That's minor.

**Applying masks to all element types adds very little work, maybe 10–20% on top of shapes only.** The renderer already clips elements this way for frames, and it doesn't care what type the element is. In the main draw loop ([staticScene.ts:345-399](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L345-L399)), each element is drawn between a save and a restore. When it belongs to a frame, `frameClip()` ([staticScene.ts:150](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L150)) clips it first. A mask clip would sit in the same place and use the mask shape's outline instead of the frame rectangle. Shapes, stamps, text, images, arrows and freehand would all be clipped by the same code.

How each element type would work out:

| Element type | Extra effort | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shapes, stamps, arrows, freehand | None | All go through the same render path. |
| Text | None | Text inside a shape is drawn in the same save/restore block as its shape, so masking the shape masks its text automatically. |
| Images | Small | They draw on the canvas normally. SVG export already gives each image its own clip ([staticSvgScene.ts:706](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L706)), so the mask's clip would wrap around it. |
| Embeds and iframes | Exclude | They're web content layered over the canvas and drawn in a separate loop, so a canvas clip won't affect them. |
| Frames, and masks themselves | Exclude | Masking a frame or a mask gets confusing fast, so I'd leave both out. |

**Work that's the same whichever types we support:**

- Building the outline for each of the four mask shapes, with rotation.
- SVG export, which needs a `<clipPath>`; frames already do this ([staticSvgScene.ts:161](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L161)).
- Clicking: by default you could still select an element by clicking a part the mask hides.
- The on/off toggle, the stored link from each element to its mask, and save/undo support.

So almost all the effort goes into those shared pieces, not into the element types. I'd recommend supporting everything except embeds and frames from the start. The extra cost is mostly a few more tests.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 20:28:22Z)**_

I've saved B to memory. The masked elements will store only a reference to their mask (something like a `maskId`) and never a copy of its position. The clip outline is rebuilt from the mask's current position, size and angle every time the canvas redraws. So moving, resizing or rotating the mask shows a different part of the content, and the content itself stays put. That matches your Q4 answer.

Two questions B doesn't settle:

1. **Is the mask shape visible?** Once a shape becomes a mask, does it keep drawing its own outline and fill as usual, or does it become invisible and only clip? An invisible mask would need some selection outline or handle so you can still find it, select it and drag it.
2. **Can one mask clip several elements?** I'm assuming yes: select some elements plus a shape, press Ctrl+Alt+G, and all of them are clipped by that shape. Each element would still have at most one mask, since combining masks is out of scope.

These can wait until C and D if they're easier to answer there.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 20:35:48Z)**_

I can see the screenshot, and it matches what we've planned. In the screenshot, "Layer 4" is the base, and the three adjustment layers above it are each clipped down to it. Mapped onto Excalidraw:

| Photoshop | Our design |
| --- | --- |
| The base layer ("Layer 4") | The mask shape, still visible |
| The clipped layers, shown with the ↓ arrow | The masked elements, each storing a reference to the mask |
| Clipped layers only show where they overlap the base | Each masked element is clipped to the mask's outline |
| Several layers clipped to one base | One mask clipping many elements |

There are two differences to keep in mind:

- **Excalidraw has no layers panel.** In Photoshop you can see the clip from the indent and the ↓ arrow. Here, the only sign that something is masked is the clipping itself. We may want a small on-canvas cue, for example highlighting the masked elements when their mask is selected. That's optional, but it would make masks easier to manage.
- **Stacking order.** Photoshop requires clipped layers to sit directly above their base. Our design doesn't need that, because the clip works wherever the elements are in the drawing order. I'd keep it that way, since it's simpler and nothing breaks when you reorder elements.

I've saved this to memory. Ready for C.

- **The mask version:** a `maskEditor` app state plus a small `MaskEditToolbar` component, rendered the same way.

While text is being edited, the canvas double-click handler stops at the top ([App.tsx:6871](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L6871)). That's where the "second double-click closes the text and opens the dialog" check would go.

Three things to confirm:

1. **Double-clicking inside the text box.** Double-clicking inside the text box normally selects a word, and people rely on that while typing. I'd suggest only a double-click on the mask _outside_ the text box closes the text and opens the dialog, while a double-click inside the box keeps selecting words. Does that work for you?
2. **What "visibility" switches.** I'm taking it to mean the clipping effect, which is criterion C. Turned off, the masked elements show in full; turned on, they're clipped again. The mask shape stays visible either way, as you said before. Is that right, rather than hiding the mask shape?
3. **One switch for the whole mask.** I'd put the on/off flag on the mask element, so one switch turns clipping on or off for every element it clips. Storing it on the element also means it's saved with the file and works with undo. Turning individual elements on and off, like Photoshop's per-layer eye icon, could come later. OK to start with the single switch?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 20:52:13Z)**_

I've saved D to memory. Removing a mask clears the mask reference on every element it clipped, so they go back to their normal appearance, and the parent becomes an ordinary shape again. Nothing is deleted, which also covers criterion E. Undo restores the mask.

Making Ctrl+Alt+G and the submenu button act as toggles raises a few cases where the selection is ambiguous:

1. **The parent plus some unmasked elements.** You select an existing mask and some elements it doesn't clip yet, then press Ctrl+Alt+G. Should it add those elements to the mask, or remove the mask? I'd suggest **add**, and remove only when the parent is selected alone or only with elements it already clips.
2. **Only clipped elements selected.** You select one or more clipped elements without the parent and press Ctrl+Alt+G. Should it release just those elements from the mask, or do nothing? Releasing them is handy and costs little, but it's beyond what D asks for.
3. **The button's label.** Should the submenu button change from "Mask" to "Remove mask" when a mask is selected, or keep one label that does whichever applies? Changing the label makes it clearer what will happen.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 21:16:45Z)**_

I've saved both answers. Objects already clipped by another mask are blocked. Allowing every type to be a parent is doable, but it changes how clipping works, so I need one decision from you.

**The problem:** the four basic shapes have a clear inside, so clipping to their outline is easy and doesn't depend on the fill. That's how we planned to do it. The other types don't have one:

| Parent type | What its "inside" would be |
| --- | --- |
| Closed line or polygon | Its enclosed area works like a shape. |
| Open line or arrow | No inside at all, only the stroke. |
| Freehand | Only the stroke itself, unless it's closed and filled. |
| Text | The letter shapes themselves. |
| Image | Its rectangle, or only its non-transparent pixels. |

**Option 1, clip to whatever the parent actually draws (pixel-based).** The parent is drawn off-screen, and children only show where it has visible pixels. This is exactly how Photoshop works, as in your screenshot, and it handles every type with one method. Text clips to the letters, an arrow to its stroke, and an image to its visible pixels.

- _Catch:_ a rectangle with a transparent fill would then clip only to its thin border. That contradicts your earlier idea of hiding a mask by setting its fill to 0; you'd have to use the shape's opacity instead, and opacity would affect the clip too.
- _Cost:_ an extra off-screen draw per mask on every frame, plus a different SVG export method (`<mask>` instead of `<clipPath>`).

**Option 2, mixed (recommended).**

- Closed shapes and closed lines clip to their outline, whatever their fill, as planned.
- Text, images, freehand and open lines or arrows clip to what they draw, using the pixel method from Option 1.
- This keeps the "transparent-fill mask" trick working for shapes, and still lets every type be a parent.
- _Cost:_ both methods have to be built, though each one is simple.

**Effort:** either option adds real work on top of the original 8 points. The pixel method is the bigger piece, mainly for SVG export and for click-testing on hidden areas. Shapes-only parents for this sprint, with the other types in a later one, is a fallback if time runs short.

Which do you prefer: Option 1, Option 2, or shapes-only for now?

Parents are back to the four basic shapes, which clip to their outline whatever their fill. Other parent types are logged in memory for a later sprint. With two days, that's the right call.

Here's the full spec as it now stands:

**Masks**

- **Parents:** rectangle, diamond, ellipse, triangle. The parent stays visible and draws normally.
- **Clippable elements:** shapes, stamps, arrows, lines, freehand, text and images. Embeds, frames and other masks are excluded.
- **How it's stored:** each clipped element holds a reference to its parent, and the parent holds an on/off flag. Clipping happens at render time, so no element's position, size or style is ever changed (E). Each element has one mask, and one mask can clip many elements.
- **Moving:** moving, resizing or rotating the parent shifts what's visible, and the clipped elements stay where they are.

**Making a mask (A)**

- Select one basic shape, then press Ctrl+Alt+G or click the Mask button, which sits directly under "Frame tool" in its submenu and keeps a single label.
- That starts masking mode:
  - Double-clicking an object marks it with an outline; double-clicking it again unmarks it.
  - Objects that can't be marked are blocked, including anything already clipped by another mask.
  - Only panning and zooming work, and text editing is blocked.
  - A bar fixed at the bottom centre reads "Currently masking", with Cancel (Excalidraw+ grey) and Done (Share style), with dark-mode colours for both.
- Done, or double-clicking empty canvas, applies the mask. Cancel or Escape throws it away.
- While masking, and while a mask is selected, the hidden parts of clipped elements show at 20% opacity.

**Double-click dialog (C, D)**

- Double-clicking the parent opens a simple dialog, the same way motion paths open their toolbar. If the shape has text, the first double-click edits the text, and the next one outside the text box opens the dialog.
- The dialog has a clipping on/off switch, an "Add elements" button that re-enters masking mode, and "Remove mask".

**Removing (D)**

- Ctrl+Alt+G or the button with the parent selected, or "Remove mask" in the dialog, removes the whole mask.
- Ctrl+Alt+G with only clipped elements selected releases just those elements.

**Also included:** SVG and PNG export, saving and reopening, and undo/redo.

Two things are deferred: the on-canvas cue for which elements are clipped (beyond the 20% preview), and the parked question of the parent selected together with unmarked elements. "Add elements" largely covers the second one.

Want me to start building, or is there anything to adjust first?

**Build plan, in order, so each step can be tested before the next:**

   - Make loading drop references to parents that no longer exist.

**How #70 avoids blocking the others:**

- The mask reference lives on each clipped element, the same pattern Excalidraw uses for `frameId` and `containerId`. That means #74 can later remap it during copy/paste, and #72 can extend it to more element types.
- The clipping is a standalone helper that #72 and #73 can reuse.
- Actions use the normal undo capture. Every Excalidraw action does this anyway, and leaving it out would make undo behave oddly. It's not the #74 persistence work.
- If a parent is deleted, a clipped element whose parent no longer exists simply draws unclipped. That's a one-line safety check to avoid crashes, not persistence work.

**Removed from our plan:**

- Images as clipped elements (#72).
- Any work or tests on mask transforms or selection (#73). Moving the mask will still shift the visible area, because that comes with the storage design, but we won't build or test anything around it.
- Load-time cleanup of missing parents, persistence tests, and copy/paste handling (#74).

SVG export and the 20% preview stay.

- **(a)** several elements, as planned, which matches #70's wording, and leaves #72 with images and editing?
- **(b)** only one element per mask, leaving all multi-element support to #72? This is simpler, but masking mode would end after one element is marked.

import { toIterable } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { isInvisiblySmallElement } from "./sizeHelpers";

import type {
  ExcalidrawElement,
  NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
  NonDeleted,
  ElementsMapOrArray,
} from "./types";

/**
 * @deprecated unsafe, use hashElementsVersion instead
 */
export const getSceneVersion = (elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[]) =>
  elements.reduce((acc, el) => acc + el.version, 0);

/**
 * Hashes elements' versionNonce (using djb2 algo). Order of elements matters.
 */
export const hashElementsVersion = (elements: ElementsMapOrArray): number => {
  let hash = 5381;
  for (const element of toIterable(elements)) {
    hash = (hash << 5) + hash + element.versionNonce;
  }
  return hash >>> 0; // Ensure unsigned 32-bit integer
};

// string hash function (using djb2). Not cryptographically secure, use only
// for versioning and such.
// note: hashes individual code units (not code points),
// but for hashing purposes this is fine as it iterates through every code unit
// (as such, no need to encode to byte string first)
export const hashString = (s: string): number => {
  let hash: number = 5381;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    const char: number = s.charCodeAt(i);
    hash = (hash << 5) + hash + char;
  }
  return hash >>> 0; // Ensure unsigned 32-bit integer
};

export const isNonDeletedElement = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  element: T,
): element is NonDeleted<T> => !element.isDeleted;

export const getVisibleElements = (
  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
): readonly NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[] =>
  elements.filter(
    (el): el is NonDeletedExcalidrawElement =>
      isNonDeletedElement(el) && !isInvisiblySmallElement(el),
  );

export const getNonDeletedElements = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
): readonly NonDeleted<T>[] => elements.filter(isNonDeletedElement);

```typescript
import { getCornerRadius } from "./utils";
import { getDiamondPoints, getTrianglePoints } from "./bounds";

import type {
  ElementsMap,
  ExcalidrawDiamondElement,
  ExcalidrawElement,
  ExcalidrawEllipseElement,
  ExcalidrawRectangleElement,
  ExcalidrawTriangleElement,
  NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
} from "./types";

export type ExcalidrawMaskElement =
  | ExcalidrawRectangleElement
  | ExcalidrawDiamondElement
  | ExcalidrawEllipseElement
  | ExcalidrawTriangleElement;

const MASK_TYPES = new Set<ExcalidrawElement["type"]>([
  "rectangle",
  "diamond",
  "ellipse",
  "triangle",
]);

// images are left to #72, embeds can't be clipped by the canvas at all
const MASKABLE_TYPES = new Set<ExcalidrawElement["type"]>([
  "rectangle",
  "diamond",
  "ellipse",
  "triangle",
  "line",
  "arrow",
  "freedraw",
  "text",
]);

/** whether the element's type can act as a mask */
export const isMaskType = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement | null | undefined,
): element is ExcalidrawMaskElement =>
  !!element && MASK_TYPES.has(element.type);

/** the mask shape clipping `element`, if it (still) exists */
export const getMaskElement = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): ExcalidrawMaskElement | null => {
  if (!element.maskId) {
    return null;
  }
  const mask = elementsMap.get(element.maskId);
  return mask && !mask.isDeleted && isMaskType(mask) ? mask : null;
};

/** the element clipped by `mask`, if any */
export const getMaskedElement = (
  mask: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): NonDeletedExcalidrawElement | null => {
  for (const element of elementsMap.values()) {
    if (element.maskId === mask.id && !element.isDeleted) {
      return element as NonDeletedExcalidrawElement;
    }
  }
  return null;
};

export const isMaskElement = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
) => isMaskType(element) && !!getMaskedElement(element, elementsMap);

export const isMaskEnabled = (mask: ExcalidrawElement) =>
  mask.maskEnabled !== false;

/** the enabled mask that should clip `element` when rendering */
export const getActiveMaskElement = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
) => {
  const mask = getMaskElement(element, elementsMap);
  return mask && isMaskEnabled(mask) ? mask : null;
};

/** whether `element` can become a mask's parent shape */
export const canBecomeMask = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
) =>
  isMaskType(element) &&
  !element.locked &&
  !getMaskElement(element, elementsMap) &&
  !isMaskElement(element, elementsMap);

/** whether `element` can be clipped by `mask` */
export const canBeMasked = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  mask: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
) =>
  element.id !== mask.id &&
  !element.isDeleted &&
  !element.locked &&
  MASKABLE_TYPES.has(element.type) &&
  // bound text is clipped together with its container
  !(element.type === "text" && element.containerId) &&
  !getMaskElement(element, elementsMap) &&
  !isMaskElement(element, elementsMap);

type MaskOutline =
  | { type: "rect"; width: number; height: number; radius: number }
  | { type: "ellipse"; width: number; height: number }
  | { type: "polygon"; points: [number, number][] };

/** the mask's outline in its local (unrotated, top-left origin) coordinates */
export const getMaskOutline = (mask: ExcalidrawMaskElement): MaskOutline => {
  const { width, height } = mask;
  switch (mask.type) {
    case "rectangle":
      return {
        type: "rect",
        width,
        height,
        radius: getCornerRadius(Math.min(width, height), mask),
      };
    case "ellipse":
      return { type: "ellipse", width, height };
    case "diamond": {
      const [tx, ty, rx, ry, bx, by, lx, ly] = getDiamondPoints(mask);
      return {
        type: "polygon",
        points: [
          [tx, ty],
          [rx, ry],
          [bx, by],
          [lx, ly],
        ],
      };
    }
    case "triangle": {
      const [tx, ty, rx, ry, lx, ly] = getTrianglePoints(mask);
      return {
        type: "polygon",
        points: [
          [tx, ty],
          [rx, ry],
          [lx, ly],
        ],
      };
    }
  }
};

/**
 * Clips the context to the mask's outline. The context is expected to be in
 * scene coordinates offset by (`offsetX`, `offsetY`), e.g. the scroll.
 */
export const clipToMask = (
  context: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  mask: ExcalidrawMaskElement,
  offsetX: number,
  offsetY: number,
) => {
  const cx = mask.x + mask.width / 2 + offsetX;
  const cy = mask.y + mask.height / 2 + offsetY;

  context.translate(cx, cy);
  context.rotate(mask.angle);
  context.translate(-mask.width / 2, -mask.height / 2);

  context.beginPath();
  const outline = getMaskOutline(mask);
  if (outline.type === "rect") {
    if (outline.radius && context.roundRect) {
      context.roundRect(0, 0, outline.width, outline.height, outline.radius);
    } else {
      context.rect(0, 0, outline.width, outline.height);
    }
  } else if (outline.type === "ellipse") {
    context.ellipse(
      outline.width / 2,
      outline.height / 2,
      outline.width / 2,
      outline.height / 2,
      0,
      0,
      Math.PI * 2,
    );
  } else {
    outline.points.forEach(([x, y], index) =>
      index ? context.lineTo(x, y) : context.moveTo(x, y),
    );
    context.closePath();
  }
  context.clip();

  context.translate(mask.width / 2, mask.height / 2);
  context.rotate(-mask.angle);
  context.translate(-cx, -cy);
};

/** SVG path data of the mask's outline, in its local coordinates */
export const getMaskSvgPathData = (mask: ExcalidrawMaskElement) => {
  const outline = getMaskOutline(mask);
  if (outline.type === "rect") {
    const { width: w, height: h } = outline;
    const r = Math.min(outline.radius, w / 2, h / 2);
    if (!r) {
      return `M0 0H${w}V${h}H0Z`;
    }
    return (
      `M${r} 0H${w - r}A${r} ${r} 0 0 1 ${w} ${r}V${h - r}` +
      `A${r} ${r} 0 0 1 ${w - r} ${h}H${r}A${r} ${r} 0 0 1 0 ${h - r}` +
      `V${r}A${r} ${r} 0 0 1 ${r} 0Z`
    );
  }
  if (outline.type === "ellipse") {
    const rx = outline.width / 2;
    const ry = outline.height / 2;
    return (
      `M0 ${ry}A${rx} ${ry} 0 1 0 ${outline.width} ${ry}` +
      `A${rx} ${ry} 0 1 0 0 ${ry}Z`
    );
  }
  return `${outline.points
    .map(([x, y], index) => `${index ? "L" : "M"}${x} ${y}`)
    .join("")}Z`;
};

/** SVG transform placing the mask's local outline into scene coordinates */
export const getMaskSvgTransform = (
  mask: ExcalidrawMaskElement,
  offsetX: number,
  offsetY: number,
) => {
  const cx = mask.x + mask.width / 2 + offsetX;
  const cy = mask.y + mask.height / 2 + offsetY;
  const degrees = (180 * mask.angle) / Math.PI;
  return `translate(${cx} ${cy}) rotate(${degrees}) translate(${
    -mask.width / 2
  } ${-mask.height / 2})`;
};

  NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import type { RoughCanvas } from "roughjs/bin/canvas";

import type {
  RenderableElementsMap,
  StaticCanvasRenderConfig,
} from "../scene/types";
import type { StaticCanvasAppState } from "../types";

/** opacity of the masked-out content previewed while the mask is selected */
export const MASK_PREVIEW_OPACITY = 0.2;

/**
 * Clips the context to the element's mask, if it has an enabled one.
 * While the mask is selected, the masked-out parts are first drawn faintly
 * so the user can see what the mask is hiding.
 */
export const applyMaskClip = (
  element: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: RenderableElementsMap,
  allElementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
  rc: RoughCanvas,
  context: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  renderConfig: StaticCanvasRenderConfig,
  appState: StaticCanvasAppState,
) => {
  const mask = getActiveMaskElement(element, allElementsMap);
  if (!mask) {
    return;
  }

  if (!renderConfig.isExporting && appState.selectedElementIds[mask.id]) {
    const boundTextElement = getBoundTextElement(element, elementsMap);
    for (const el of boundTextElement
      ? [element, boundTextElement]
      : [element]) {
      renderElement(
        el,
        elementsMap,
        allElementsMap,
        rc,
        context,
        renderConfig,
        appState,
        MASK_PREVIEW_OPACITY,
      );
    }
  }

  clipToMask(context, mask, appState.scrollX, appState.scrollY);
};
```

60	 * Commits a motion-path edit session: the path keeps its edited geometry and
61	 * its target(s) are snapped onto the (possibly moved) start point — the same
62	 * rule applied when a path is first confirmed (see actionFinalize.tsx).
63	 */
64	export const actionFinishMotionPathEdit = register({
65	  name: "finishMotionPathEdit",
66	  label: "labels.pathEditor.done",
67	  trackEvent: false,
68	  predicate: (elements, appState) => !!appState.motionPathEditor,
69	  perform: (elements, appState) => {
70	    const path = getEditedPath(elements, appState);
71	    if (!path) {
72	      return {
73	        appState: exitedAppState(appState),
74	        captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
75	      };
76	    }
77
78	    return {
79	      elements: alignPathTargetsToStart(elements, path),
80	      appState: exitedAppState(appState),
81	      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
82	    };
83	  },
84	});

86	/**
87	 * Returns `elements` with `path`'s target(s) — and their bound text — shifted
88	 * so their combined center sits on the path's motion start point.
89	 */
90	const alignPathTargetsToStart = (
91	  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
92	  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
93	): readonly ExcalidrawElement[] => {
94	  const elementsMap = arrayToMap(elements);
95	  const targets = getPathTargetElements(path, elementsMap);
96	  const offset = getPathAlignmentOffset(path, targets, elementsMap);
97	  if (offset.x === 0 && offset.y === 0) {
98	    return elements;
99	  }
100
101	  const shiftedIds = new Set<string>();
102	  for (const target of targets) {
103	    shiftedIds.add(target.id);
104	    const boundText = getBoundTextElement(target, elementsMap);
105	    if (boundText) {
106	      shiftedIds.add(boundText.id);
107	    }
108	  }
109
110	  return elements.map((el) =>
111	    shiftedIds.has(el.id)
112	      ? newElementWith(el, {
113	          x: el.x + offset.x,
114	          y: el.y + offset.y,
115	        })
116	      : el,
117	  );
118	};

120	/**
121	 * Restores the path and its target(s) to exactly how they were when the edit
122	 * session started, and leaves edit mode. Shared with `actionDeleteSelected`
123	 * (Delete with no points selected rejects), since only one action may match
124	 * a given key.
125	 */
126	export const rejectMotionPathEdit = (
127	  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
128	  appState: Readonly<AppState>,
129	): ActionResult => {
130	  const { motionPathEditor } = appState;
131	  if (!motionPathEditor) {
132	    return false;
133	  }
134	  const { original, originalPositions } = motionPathEditor;
135
136	  return {
137	    elements: elements.map((el) => {
138	      if (el.id === original.id && isPathElement(el)) {
139	        return newElementWith(el, {
140	          x: original.x,
141	          y: original.y,
142	          width: original.width,
143	          height: original.height,
144	          angle: original.angle,
145	          points: original.points,
146	          roundness: original.roundness,
147	          motion: original.motion,
148	        });
149	      }
150	      const position = originalPositions[el.id];
151	      if (position && (el.x !== position.x || el.y !== position.y)) {
152	        return newElementWith(el, position);
153	      }
154	      return el;
155	    }),
156	    appState: exitedAppState(appState),
157	    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
158	  };
159	};

164	  trackEvent: false,

177	  perform: (elements, appState) => {
178	    const path = getEditedPath(elements, appState);
179	    if (!path) {
180	      return false;
181	    }
182	    return {
183	      elements: elements.map((el) =>
184	        el.id === path.id
185	          ? newElementWith(el, {

187	                ? null
188	                : { type: ROUNDNESS.PROPORTIONAL_RADIUS },
189	            })

191	      ),

198	/**
199	 * Updates the edited path's movement config (speed, easing, start/end).
200	 * `value` is merged over the current config and normalized, so start/end can
201	 * never cross. When the start moves, the target is re-snapped onto it so it
202	 * keeps resting where playback will begin.
203	 */
204	export const actionChangeMotionPathConfig = register<Partial<PathMotionConfig>>(
205	  {
206	    name: "changeMotionPathConfig",
207	    label: "labels.pathEditor.motion",
208	    trackEvent: false,
209	    predicate: (elements, appState) => !!getEditedPath(elements, appState),
210	    perform: (elements, appState, value) => {
211	      const path = getEditedPath(elements, appState);
212	      if (!path || !value) {
213	        return false;
214	      }
215	      const motion = normalizePathMotion({ ...path.motion, ...value });
216	      const updatedPath = newElementWith(path, { motion });
217	      const nextElements = elements.map((el) =>
218	        el.id === path.id ? updatedPath : el,
219	      );
220	      return {
221	        elements:
222	          motion.start !== path.motion.start
223	            ? alignPathTargetsToStart(nextElements, updatedPath)
224	            : nextElements,
225	        appState,
226	        captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
227	      };
228	    },
229	  },
230	);

232	/**
233	 * Re-opens a confirmed motion path for editing: point editing via the
234	 * (already path-aware) LinearElementEditor, plus move/resize/rotate handles
235	 * kept visible for the path while editing (see hasBoundingBox). The path and
236	 * its target(s) are snapshotted so the whole session can be rejected.
237	 */
238	export const actionEditMotionPath = register({
239	  name: "editMotionPath",
240	  label: "labels.pathEditor.edit",
241	  icon: PathIcon,
242	  category: DEFAULT_CATEGORIES.elements,
243	  keywords: ["motion", "path", "animation"],
244	  trackEvent: { category: "element" },
245	  predicate: (elements, appState, _, app) => {
246	    const selectedElements = app.scene.getSelectedElements(appState);
247	    return (
248	      selectedElements.length === 1 &&
249	      isPathElement(selectedElements[0]) &&
250	      !selectedElements[0].locked &&
251	      appState.motionPathEditor?.pathId !== selectedElements[0].id
252	    );
253	  },
254	  perform: (elements, appState, _, app: AppClassProperties) => {
255	    const [path] = app.scene.getSelectedElements(appState);
256	    if (!path || !isPathElement(path)) {
257	      return false;
258	    }
259
260	    const elementsMap = app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap();
261	    const originalPositions: Record<string, { x: number; y: number }> = {};
262	    for (const target of getPathTargetElements(path, elementsMap)) {
263	      originalPositions[target.id] = { x: target.x, y: target.y };
264	      const boundText = getBoundTextElement(target, elementsMap);
265	      if (boundText) {
266	        originalPositions[boundText.id] = { x: boundText.x, y: boundText.y };
267	      }
268	    }
269
270	    return {
271	      appState: {
272	        ...appState,
273	        selectedLinearElement: new LinearElementEditor(
274	          path as NonDeleted<ExcalidrawPathElement>,
275	          elementsMap,
276	          true,
277	        ),
278	        motionPathEditor: {
279	          pathId: path.id,
280	          // a copy, not the live element: edits mutate the scene element
281	          // in place, which would otherwise rewrite the snapshot too
282	          // (`points` arrays are replaced on edit, never mutated, so a
283	          // shallow copy is enough)
284	          original: { ...path },
285	          originalPositions,
286	        },
287	      },
288	      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
289	    };
290	  },
291	});

export type DropdownMenuItemProps = {

  value?: string | number | undefined;

  children: React.ReactNode;

const DropdownMenuItem = ({

  const handleSelect = useHandleDropdownMenuItemSelect(onSelect);

  return (
    <DropdownMenuPrimitive.Item
      className="radix-menu-item"
      onSelect={handleSelect}
      asChild
    >
      <button
        {...rest}
        value={value}
        className={getDropdownMenuItemClassName(className, selected)}
        title={rest.title ?? rest["aria-label"]}
      >
        <MenuItemContent icon={icon} shortcut={shortcut} badge={badge}>
          {children}
        </MenuItemContent>
      </button>
    </DropdownMenuPrimitive.Item>
  );
};
DropdownMenuItem.displayName = "DropdownMenuItem";

  GREEN: "green",
  RED: "red",
  BLUE: "blue",
} as const;

```typescript
import {
  canBeMasked,
  canBecomeMask,
  getMaskedElement,
  getMaskElement,
  isMaskElement,
  isMaskEnabled,
  newElementWith,
  CaptureUpdateAction,
} from "@excalidraw/element";
import { arrayToMap, CODES, KEYS } from "@excalidraw/common";

import type { ElementsMap, ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { DEFAULT_CATEGORIES } from "../components/CommandPalette/CommandPalette";
import { MaskIcon } from "../components/icons";

import { register } from "./register";

import type { AppClassProperties, AppState } from "../types";

type MaskActionType = "start" | "remove" | "release";

/**
 * What the mask shortcut/button does for the current selection:
 * - `start`: a single shape that can become a mask → enter masking mode
 * - `remove`: a single mask shape → remove its mask
 * - `release`: only masked elements → release them from their masks
 */
export const getMaskActionType = (
  selectedElements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): MaskActionType | null => {
  if (!selectedElements.length) {
    return null;
  }
  if (selectedElements.length === 1) {
    const [element] = selectedElements;
    if (isMaskElement(element, elementsMap)) {
      return "remove";
    }
    if (canBecomeMask(element, elementsMap)) {
      return "start";
    }
  }
  if (selectedElements.every((el) => getMaskElement(el, elementsMap))) {
    return "release";
  }
  return null;
};

/** the mask the open mask editor belongs to, if it still exists */
export const getEditedMask = (
  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
  appState: Readonly<Pick<AppState, "maskEditor">>,
) => {
  if (!appState.maskEditor) {
    return null;
  }
  const mask = elements.find((el) => el.id === appState.maskEditor!.maskId);
  return mask && !mask.isDeleted ? mask : null;
};

/** clears the mask fields so the elements render unmasked again */
const unmaskElements = (
  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
  ids: ReadonlySet<string>,
) =>
  elements.map((el) =>
    ids.has(el.id)
      ? newElementWith(el, { maskId: undefined, maskEnabled: undefined })
      : el,
  );

const exitedAppState = (appState: Readonly<AppState>): AppState => ({
  ...appState,
  maskEditor: null,
});

export const actionToggleMask = register({
  name: "toggleMask",
  label: "labels.mask.toggle",
  icon: MaskIcon,
  category: DEFAULT_CATEGORIES.elements,
  keywords: ["mask", "clip", "clipping"],
  trackEvent: { category: "element" },
  predicate: (elements, appState, _, app) =>
    appState.maskEditor?.mode === "picking" ||
    !!getMaskActionType(
      app.scene.getSelectedElements(appState),
      app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap(),
    ),
  perform: (elements, appState, _, app: AppClassProperties) => {
    // pressing it again while picking cancels masking mode
    if (appState.maskEditor?.mode === "picking") {
      return {
        appState: exitedAppState(appState),
        captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
      };
    }

    const elementsMap = app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap();
    const selectedElements = app.scene.getSelectedElements(appState);

    switch (getMaskActionType(selectedElements, elementsMap)) {
      case "start":
        return {
          appState: {
            ...appState,
            maskEditor: { maskId: selectedElements[0].id, mode: "picking" },
          },
          captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
        };
      case "remove": {
        const [mask] = selectedElements;
        const masked = getMaskedElement(mask, elementsMap);
        return {
          elements: unmaskElements(
            elements,
            new Set(masked ? [mask.id, masked.id] : [mask.id]),
          ),
          appState: exitedAppState(appState),
          captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
        };
      }
      case "release":
        return {
          elements: unmaskElements(
            elements,
            new Set(selectedElements.map((el) => el.id)),
          ),
          appState,
          captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
        };
      default:
        return false;
    }
  },
  keyTest: (event) =>
    event[KEYS.CTRL_OR_CMD] &&
    event.altKey &&
    !event.shiftKey &&
    // `event.key` is a special character with Alt held on some layouts
    event.code === CODES.G,
});

/** masking mode: clips the element with id `value` to the mask being picked */
export const actionApplyMask = register<ExcalidrawElement["id"]>({
  name: "applyMask",
  label: "labels.mask.toggle",
  trackEvent: false,
  predicate: (elements, appState) => appState.maskEditor?.mode === "picking",
  perform: (elements, appState, value) => {
    const mask = getEditedMask(elements, appState);
    const elementsMap = arrayToMap(elements);
    const target = value ? elementsMap.get(value) : undefined;
    if (
      appState.maskEditor?.mode !== "picking" ||
      !mask ||
      !target ||
      !canBeMasked(target, mask, elementsMap)
    ) {
      return false;
    }
    return {
      elements: elements.map((el) =>
        el.id === target.id ? newElementWith(el, { maskId: mask.id }) : el,
      ),
      appState: {
        ...exitedAppState(appState),
        selectedElementIds: { [mask.id]: true },
        selectedGroupIds: {},
      },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
    };
  },
});

export const actionCancelMasking = register({
  name: "cancelMasking",
  label: "buttons.cancel",
  trackEvent: false,
  predicate: (elements, appState) => appState.maskEditor?.mode === "picking",
  perform: (elements, appState) => ({
    appState: exitedAppState(appState),
    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
  }),
});

/** opens the mask's options (double-clicking a mask shape) */
export const actionEditMask = register({
  name: "editMask",
  label: "labels.mask.edit",
  trackEvent: false,
  predicate: (elements, appState, _, app) => {
    const selectedElements = app.scene.getSelectedElements(appState);
    return (
      selectedElements.length === 1 &&
      isMaskElement(selectedElements[0], app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap())
    );
  },
  perform: (elements, appState, _, app: AppClassProperties) => {
    const [mask] = app.scene.getSelectedElements(appState);
    if (!mask || !isMaskElement(mask, app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap())) {
      return false;
    }
    return {
      appState: {
        ...appState,
        maskEditor: { maskId: mask.id, mode: "editing" },
      },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
    };
  },
});

export const actionCloseMaskEditor = register({
  name: "closeMaskEditor",
  label: "buttons.close",
  trackEvent: false,
  predicate: (elements, appState) => appState.maskEditor?.mode === "editing",
  perform: (elements, appState) => ({
    appState: exitedAppState(appState),
    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
  }),
});

/** turns the edited mask's clipping on or off, keeping the masked element */
export const actionToggleMaskEnabled = register({
  name: "toggleMaskEnabled",
  label: "labels.mask.enabled",
  trackEvent: false,
  predicate: (elements, appState) => !!getEditedMask(elements, appState),
  perform: (elements, appState) => {
    const mask = getEditedMask(elements, appState);
    if (!mask) {
      return false;
    }
    return {
      elements: elements.map((el) =>
        el.id === mask.id
          ? newElementWith(el, { maskEnabled: !isMaskEnabled(mask) })
          : el,
      ),
      appState,
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
    };
  },
});

/** removes the edited mask, restoring its element's unmasked appearance */
export const actionRemoveMask = register({
  name: "removeMask",
  label: "labels.mask.remove",
  trackEvent: false,
  predicate: (elements, appState) => !!getEditedMask(elements, appState),
  perform: (elements, appState) => {
    const mask = getEditedMask(elements, appState);
    if (!mask) {
      return false;
    }
    const ids = new Set([mask.id]);
    for (const el of elements) {
      if (el.maskId === mask.id) {
        ids.add(el.id);
      }
    }
    return {
      elements: unmaskElements(elements, ids),
      appState: exitedAppState(appState),
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
    };
  },
});
```

import { vi } from "vitest";

import { arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";

import {
  canBeMasked,
  canBecomeMask,
  getActiveMaskElement,
  getMaskElement,
  getMaskSvgPathData,
  isMaskElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { Radians } from "@excalidraw/math";

import type {
  ExcalidrawElement,
  NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { getDefaultAppState } from "../appState";
import { exportToCanvas, exportToSvg } from "../scene/export";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";

const createMasked = (
  mask: ExcalidrawElement,
  type: "rectangle" | "freedraw" | "text" = "rectangle",
) =>
  ({
    ...API.createElement({ type, x: 50, y: 50, width: 100, height: 100 }),
    maskId: mask.id,
  } as NonDeletedExcalidrawElement);

describe("mask lookup", () => {
  it("finds the mask of a masked element", () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "ellipse" });
    const masked = createMasked(mask);
    const elementsMap = arrayToMap([mask, masked]);

    expect(getMaskElement(masked, elementsMap)?.id).toBe(mask.id);
    expect(getActiveMaskElement(masked, elementsMap)?.id).toBe(mask.id);
    expect(isMaskElement(mask, elementsMap)).toBe(true);
    expect(isMaskElement(masked, elementsMap)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("ignores a disabled mask when rendering, but keeps the relationship", () => {
    const mask = {
      ...API.createElement({ type: "diamond" }),
      maskEnabled: false,
    };
    const masked = createMasked(mask);
    const elementsMap = arrayToMap([mask, masked]);

    expect(getMaskElement(masked, elementsMap)?.id).toBe(mask.id);
    expect(getActiveMaskElement(masked, elementsMap)).toBe(null);
  });

  it("ignores a deleted or missing mask", () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", isDeleted: true });
    const masked = createMasked(mask);

    expect(getMaskElement(masked, arrayToMap([mask, masked]))).toBe(null);
    expect(getMaskElement(masked, arrayToMap([masked]))).toBe(null);
  });

  it("only treats basic shapes as masks", () => {
    const line = API.createElement({ type: "line" });
    const masked = createMasked(line);

    expect(getMaskElement(masked, arrayToMap([line, masked]))).toBe(null);
  });
});

describe("mask eligibility", () => {
  it("lets basic shapes become masks", () => {
    for (const type of [
      "rectangle",
      "diamond",
      "ellipse",
      "triangle",
    ] as const) {
      const element = API.createElement({ type });
      expect(canBecomeMask(element, arrayToMap([element]))).toBe(true);
    }
    for (const type of ["line", "arrow", "freedraw", "text"] as const) {
      const element = API.createElement({ type });
      expect(canBecomeMask(element, arrayToMap([element]))).toBe(false);
    }
  });

  it("doesn't let masks or masked elements become masks", () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
    const masked = createMasked(mask);
    const elementsMap = arrayToMap([mask, masked]);

    expect(canBecomeMask(mask, elementsMap)).toBe(false);
    expect(canBecomeMask(masked, elementsMap)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("lets shapes, lines, arrows, freedraw and text be masked", () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
    for (const type of [
      "rectangle",
      "diamond",
      "ellipse",
      "triangle",
      "line",
      "arrow",
      "freedraw",
      "text",
    ] as const) {
      const element = API.createElement({ type });
      expect(canBeMasked(element, mask, arrayToMap([mask, element]))).toBe(
        true,
      );
    }
  });

  it("doesn't let images, frames or embeds be masked", () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
    for (const type of ["image", "frame", "embeddable"] as const) {
      const element = API.createElement({ type });
      expect(canBeMasked(element, mask, arrayToMap([mask, element]))).toBe(
        false,
      );
    }
  });

  it("doesn't let the mask itself, other masks or masked elements be masked", () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
    const otherMask = API.createElement({ type: "ellipse" });
    const otherMasked = createMasked(otherMask);
    const elementsMap = arrayToMap([mask, otherMask, otherMasked]);

    expect(canBeMasked(mask, mask, elementsMap)).toBe(false);
    expect(canBeMasked(otherMask, mask, elementsMap)).toBe(false);
    expect(canBeMasked(otherMasked, mask, elementsMap)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("doesn't let locked elements or bound text be masked", () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
    const locked = API.createElement({ type: "ellipse", locked: true });
    const boundText = API.createElement({
      type: "text",
      containerId: "container",
    });
    const elementsMap = arrayToMap([mask, locked, boundText]);

    expect(canBeMasked(locked, mask, elementsMap)).toBe(false);
    expect(canBeMasked(boundText, mask, elementsMap)).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("mask outline", () => {
  it("traces each basic shape", () => {
    expect(
      getMaskSvgPathData(
        API.createElement({
          type: "rectangle",
          width: 100,
          height: 50,
          roundness: null,
        }),
      ),
    ).toBe("M0 0H100V50H0Z");
    expect(
      getMaskSvgPathData(
        API.createElement({ type: "triangle", width: 100, height: 50 }),
      ),
    ).toBe("M51 0L100 50L0 50Z");
    expect(
      getMaskSvgPathData(
        API.createElement({ type: "diamond", width: 100, height: 50 }),
      ),
    ).toBe("M51 0L100 26L51 50L0 26Z");
    expect(
      getMaskSvgPathData(
        API.createElement({ type: "ellipse", width: 100, height: 50 }),
      ),
    ).toBe("M0 25A50 25 0 1 0 100 25A50 25 0 1 0 0 25Z");
  });

  it("rounds a rounded rectangle's corners", () => {
    const path = getMaskSvgPathData(
      API.createElement({
        type: "rectangle",
        width: 100,
        height: 100,
        roundness: { type: 3 },
      }),
    );
    expect(path).toContain("A");
  });
});

describe("mask PNG export", () => {
  const exportClipCalls = async (elements: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) => {
    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    const context = canvas.getContext("2d")!;
    const clip = vi.spyOn(context, "clip");

    await exportToCanvas(
      elements,
      {
        ...getDefaultAppState(),
        // layout fields, unused by export
        width: 0,
        height: 0,
        offsetTop: 0,
        offsetLeft: 0,
        exportScale: 1,
      },
      {},
      { exportBackground: false, viewBackgroundColor: "#ffffff" },
      (width, height) => {
        canvas.width = width;
        canvas.height = height;
        return { canvas, scale: 1 };
      },
    );
    return clip.mock.calls.length;
  };

  it("clips a masked element to its mask", async () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({
      type: "ellipse",
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
    });
    for (const type of ["rectangle", "freedraw", "text"] as const) {
      expect(await exportClipCalls([mask, createMasked(mask, type)])).toBe(1);
    }
  });

  it("doesn't clip when the mask is disabled or gone", async () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "ellipse" });
    const disabled = { ...mask, maskEnabled: false };

    expect(await exportClipCalls([disabled, createMasked(disabled)])).toBe(0);
    expect(await exportClipCalls([createMasked(mask)])).toBe(0);
  });

  it("doesn't clip unmasked elements", async () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({ type: "ellipse" });
    const other = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });

    expect(await exportClipCalls([mask, createMasked(mask), other])).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe("mask SVG export", () => {
  const exportSvg = (elements: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) =>
    exportToSvg(
      elements,
      { exportBackground: false, viewBackgroundColor: "#ffffff" },
      null,
      { skipInliningFonts: true },
    );

  it("wraps a masked element in a group clipped to its mask", async () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({
      type: "triangle",
      width: 100,
      height: 50,
    });
    const masked = createMasked(mask);
    const svg = await exportSvg([mask, masked]);

    const clipPath = svg.querySelector(`#mask-clipPath-${masked.id}`);
    expect(clipPath?.querySelector("path")?.getAttribute("d")).toBe(
      "M51 0L100 50L0 50Z",
    );

    const group = svg.querySelector(
      `g[clip-path="url(#mask-clipPath-${masked.id})"]`,
    );
    expect(group?.querySelector(`[data-id="${masked.id}"]`)).not.toBe(null);
    // the mask itself is rendered normally, outside the clipped group
    expect(group?.querySelector(`[data-id="${mask.id}"]`)).toBe(null);
    expect(svg.querySelector(`[data-id="${mask.id}"]`)).not.toBe(null);
  });

  it("follows the mask's rotation", async () => {
    const mask = API.createElement({
      type: "rectangle",
      width: 100,
      height: 50,
      angle: (Math.PI / 2) as Radians,
    });
    const masked = createMasked(mask);
    const svg = await exportSvg([mask, masked]);

    const transform = svg
      .querySelector(`#mask-clipPath-${masked.id} path`)
      ?.getAttribute("transform");
    expect(transform).toContain("rotate(90)");
  });

  it("doesn't clip when the mask is disabled", async () => {
    const mask = {
      ...API.createElement({ type: "ellipse" }),
      maskEnabled: false,
    };
    const masked = createMasked(mask);
    const svg = await exportSvg([mask, masked]);

    expect(svg.querySelector(`#mask-clipPath-${masked.id}`)).toBe(null);
  });
});

---

## Step 1: Data model + clipping. **Done.**

**Goal:** an element that references a mask is drawn clipped to that mask's outline, on the canvas and in exports.

**Changes:**

- [types.ts](packages/element/src/types.ts) gets two optional element fields:
  - `maskId` on the clipped element;
  - `maskEnabled` on the parent. Treated as on unless it's `false`.
- [restore.ts](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts): a typing change only, so loading keeps the two fields. No cleanup logic, since that's #74.
- New file [mask.ts](packages/element/src/mask.ts) with:
  - the rules: the four parent types, which elements can be clipped, and which can become a parent;
  - lookups between an element and its mask;
  - building the outline for each shape, including rotation and rounded corners;
  - the canvas clip and the SVG path.
- [renderElement.ts](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts): an optional opacity multiplier, used for the preview.
- New file [maskClip.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/maskClip.ts) does three things:
  - applies the canvas clip;
  - draws the 20% preview while the parent is selected, never in exports;
  - builds the SVG clipped group.
- [staticScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts) and [staticSvgScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts): a few lines that hook `maskClip.ts` in. These are kept small because CashenCroft's open PR #116 edits the same loop.

**Check:** [mask.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/mask.test.tsx) has 18 tests, and all pass:

- the lookup and eligibility rules;
- the outline for each shape;
- PNG clipping with the mask on, off or missing;
- the SVG clip path, its rotation, and the off case.

The existing gradient and export tests still pass.

---

## Step 2: Actions + shortcut

**Goal:** every mask operation exists as an action, so the shortcut, the button and the dialog all use the same code.

**Changes:**

- New file `actions/actionMask.tsx`. It's already drafted, but not tested yet.
  - `toggleMask` runs on Ctrl+Alt+G and the toolbar button. It checks the physical G key, because Option+G types `©` on Mac. It acts on the selection:
    - one basic shape → enter masking mode;
    - one parent → remove its mask;
    - only clipped elements → release them;
    - while picking → cancel.
  - `applyMask` clips the picked element and turns the mask on. Ineligible elements are refused.
  - `cancelMasking` leaves masking mode without changing anything.
  - `editMask` and `closeMaskEditor` open and close the dialog.
  - `toggleMaskEnabled` is the clipping on/off switch.
  - `removeMask` is the dialog's Remove button.
- Supporting changes:
  - `maskEditor` app state in `types.ts` and `appState.ts`, never saved and never in history;
  - register the action names, add the shortcut to the help list, and add `CODES.G` and the English strings.
- Fix the two typing errors in the half-finished `App.tsx` key handling, which I tried just now. Without that fix, nothing passes the typecheck.

**Check:** new tests in `mask.test.tsx`:

- each selection case does the right thing;
- Ctrl+Alt+G triggers it, and Ctrl+G still groups;
- toggle, remove and release leave position, size and style untouched (criterion E);
- undo and redo restore each change;
- the typecheck passes.

---

## Step 3: Masking mode

**Goal:** the picking flow in the app.

**Changes:**

- `App.tsx`:
  - the keyboard: Escape or Ctrl+Alt+G cancels, zoom keys and Space pass through, and everything else is blocked. This is partly in place.
  - pointer-down: only panning works. This was the edit you stopped.
  - double-click:
    - an eligible element → apply;
    - empty canvas → cancel;
    - an ineligible element → ignored.
  - leave masking mode if the tool changes or the parent is deleted.
- New `MaskingModeBar` component:
  - fixed at the bottom centre, in the top toolbar's style;
  - text: "Double-click an element to mask it";
  - a Cancel button in the Excalidraw+ grey, with its colours copied into package styles, light and dark.

**Check:**

- In the app: draw a shape and another element, press Ctrl+Alt+G, double-click the other element, and it's clipped.
- Panning and zooming work while picking, and clicking or dragging does nothing.
- Tests for blocking, cancelling and applying.

---

## Step 4: Toolbar button

**Goal:** a "Mask" item directly under "Frame tool" in the More tools menu.

**Changes:**

- [Toolbar.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/Toolbar.tsx): a new menu item with the mask icon, already drawn in `icons.tsx`.
  - It shows the shortcut hint and keeps one label.
  - It's disabled when the action doesn't apply to the selection.
  - The menu just gets taller, so the style is unchanged.

**Check:** open the menu in light and dark mode, then try the button in each of the three cases: start, remove and release.

---

## Step 5: Double-click dialog

**Goal:** turning clipping on and off, and removing the mask, from the parent.

**Changes:**

- New `MaskEditToolbar` component next to the parent, modelled on `MotionPathEditToolbar`. It has a Clipping on/off switch and a Remove mask button.
- `App.tsx` double-click:
  - double-clicking a parent opens the dialog;
  - if the parent has a text box, the first double-click edits the text as usual, and the next double-click _outside_ the text box opens the dialog. Double-clicking inside the box still selects words.
- Escape or clicking elsewhere closes the dialog.

**Check:** try both paths in the app, with and without text. Tests for opening, toggling and removing.

Step 1 changed six existing files, adding 46 lines and changing 4. All the actual logic is in the two new files, `mask.ts` and `maskClip.ts`.

**[packages/element/src/types.ts:82-86](packages/element/src/types.ts#L82-L86)** adds two optional fields to every element:

```ts
/** id of the mask shape this element is clipped to */
maskId?: string | null;
/** on a mask shape: whether it currently clips its masked element
    (undefined is treated as enabled) */
maskEnabled?: boolean;
```

Because they're optional, existing elements, files and snapshots are unaffected.

**[packages/element/src/index.ts:83](packages/element/src/index.ts#L83)** exports the new module:

```ts
export * from "./mask";
```

**[packages/element/src/renderElement.ts:899-900](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts#L899-L900) and [911-913](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts#L911-L913)** add an optional opacity multiplier for the 20% preview. It defaults to 1, so every existing call behaves the same:

```ts
  appState: StaticCanvasAppState | InteractiveCanvasAppState,
+ /** extra opacity factor, e.g. for previewing masked-out content */
+ opacityMultiplier: number = 1,
...
- reduceAlphaForSelection ? DEFAULT_REDUCED_GLOBAL_ALPHA : 1,
+ (reduceAlphaForSelection ? DEFAULT_REDUCED_GLOBAL_ALPHA : 1) *
+   opacityMultiplier,
```

**[packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts:456-461](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L456-L461)** is a typing change only. Without it, the loader's type would require the two optional fields on every element. It treats them like `customData`:

```ts

+ T extends Required<
+   Omit<ExcalidrawElement, "customData" | "maskId" | "maskEnabled">
+ > & {
    customData?: ExcalidrawElement["customData"];
+   maskId?: ExcalidrawElement["maskId"];
+   maskEnabled?: ExcalidrawElement["maskEnabled"];
```

**[packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts)** handles the canvas and PNG export:

export type KeyboardModifiers = {
  alt?: boolean;
  shift?: boolean;
  ctrl?: boolean;
};
export class Keyboard {
  static withModifierKeys = (modifiers: KeyboardModifiers, cb: () => void) => {
    const prevAltKey = altKey;
    const prevShiftKey = shiftKey;
    const prevCtrlKey = ctrlKey;

    altKey = !!modifiers.alt;
    shiftKey = !!modifiers.shift;
    ctrlKey = !!modifiers.ctrl;

    try {
      cb();
    } finally {
      altKey = prevAltKey;
      shiftKey = prevShiftKey;
      ctrlKey = prevCtrlKey;
    }
  };

  static keyDown = (
    key: string,
    target: HTMLElement | Document | Window = document,
  ) => {
    fireEvent.keyDown(target, {
      key,
      ctrlKey,
      shiftKey,
      altKey,
    });
  };

  static keyUp = (
    key: string,
    target: HTMLElement | Document | Window = document,
  ) => {
    fireEvent.keyUp(target, {
      key,
      ctrlKey,
      shiftKey,
      altKey,
    });
  };

  static keyPress = (key: string, target?: HTMLElement | Document | Window) => {
    Keyboard.keyDown(key, target);
    Keyboard.keyUp(key, target);
  };

  static codeDown = (code: string) => {
    fireEvent.keyDown(document, {
      code,
      ctrlKey,
      shiftKey,
      altKey,
    });
  };

  static codeUp = (code: string) => {
    fireEvent.keyUp(document, {
      code,
      ctrlKey,
      shiftKey,
      altKey,
    });
  };

  static codePress = (code: string) => {
    Keyboard.codeDown(code);
    Keyboard.codeUp(code);
  };

```typescript
import React from "react";

import { CODES, KEYS } from "@excalidraw/common";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import {
  actionApplyMask,
  actionEditMask,
  actionRemoveMask,
  actionToggleMaskEnabled,
} from "../actions";
import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Keyboard } from "./helpers/ui";
import { act, fireEvent, render, unmountComponent } from "./test-utils";

const { h } = window;

/** Ctrl+Alt+G; `key` is what the layout produces, e.g. "©" for Option+G */
const pressMaskShortcut = (key = KEYS.G) => {
  fireEvent.keyDown(document, {
    key,
    code: CODES.G,
    ctrlKey: true,
    altKey: true,
  });
};

const applyMask = (element: ExcalidrawElement) => {
  act(() => {
    h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionApplyMask, "api", element.id);
  });
};

/** the element's content, i.e. everything but its mask fields and versioning */
const content = (element: ExcalidrawElement) => {
  const { maskId, maskEnabled, version, versionNonce, updated, ...rest } =
    API.getElement(element);
  return rest;
};

const setup = () => {
  const mask = API.createElement({
    type: "ellipse",
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    width: 100,
    height: 100,
  });
  const target = API.createElement({
    type: "rectangle",
    x: 50,
    y: 50,
    width: 100,
    height: 100,
    backgroundColor: "#ffc9c9",
  });
  API.setElements([mask, target]);
  return { mask, target };
};

/** masks `target` with `mask` the way the user does */
const createMask = (mask: ExcalidrawElement, target: ExcalidrawElement) => {
  API.setSelectedElements([mask]);
  pressMaskShortcut();
  applyMask(target);
};

beforeEach(async () => {
  unmountComponent();
  await render(<Excalidraw autoFocus={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
});

describe("mask shortcut", () => {
  it("enters masking mode for a single basic shape", () => {
    const { mask } = setup();
    API.setSelectedElements([mask]);

    pressMaskShortcut();

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toEqual({ maskId: mask.id, mode: "picking" });
  });

  it("works when Alt changes the typed character (macOS)", () => {
    const { mask } = setup();
    API.setSelectedElements([mask]);

    pressMaskShortcut("©");

    expect(h.state.maskEditor?.maskId).toBe(mask.id);
  });

  it("cancels masking mode when pressed again", () => {
    const { mask } = setup();
    API.setSelectedElements([mask]);

    pressMaskShortcut();
    pressMaskShortcut();

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });

  it("does nothing for shapes that can't be masks", () => {
    const line = API.createElement({ type: "line" });
    API.setElements([line]);
    API.setSelectedElements([line]);

    pressMaskShortcut();

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });

  it("does nothing for several unmasked elements, and doesn't group them", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    API.setSelectedElements([mask, target]);

    pressMaskShortcut();

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect(API.getElement(mask).groupIds).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("leaves Ctrl+G grouping working", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    API.setSelectedElements([mask, target]);

    Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
    });

    expect(API.getElement(mask).groupIds).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});

describe("applying a mask", () => {
  it("clips the picked element and selects the mask", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();

    createMask(mask, target);

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);
    expect(API.getElement(mask).maskEnabled).toBe(true);
    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [mask.id]: true });
  });

  it("doesn't change the masked element's content", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    const before = [content(mask), content(target)];

    createMask(mask, target);

    expect([content(mask), content(target)]).toEqual(before);
  });

  it("refuses elements that can't be masked", () => {
    const { mask } = setup();
    const image = API.createElement({ type: "image" });
    API.setElements([...h.elements, image]);
    API.setSelectedElements([mask]);
    pressMaskShortcut();

    applyMask(image);

    expect(API.getElement(image).maskId).toBeUndefined();
    expect(h.state.maskEditor?.mode).toBe("picking");
  });

  it("refuses an element that is already masked", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);
    const otherMask = API.createElement({ type: "diamond" });
    API.setElements([...h.elements, otherMask]);
    API.setSelectedElements([otherMask]);
    pressMaskShortcut();

    applyMask(target);

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);
  });

  it("is undoable", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBeFalsy();

    Keyboard.redo();
    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);
  });
});

describe("removing and releasing masks", () => {
  it("removes the mask when the shortcut is pressed on it", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);
    const before = [content(mask), content(target)];

    API.setSelectedElements([API.getElement(mask)]);
    pressMaskShortcut();

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(null);
    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect([content(mask), content(target)]).toEqual(before);
  });

  it("releases masked elements when only they are selected", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);

    API.setSelectedElements([API.getElement(target)]);
    pressMaskShortcut();

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(null);
  });

  it("can undo removing a mask", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);
    API.setSelectedElements([API.getElement(mask)]);
    pressMaskShortcut();

    Keyboard.undo();

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);
  });
});

describe("mask options", () => {
  const openOptions = (mask: ExcalidrawElement) => {
    API.setSelectedElements([API.getElement(mask)]);
    API.executeAction(actionEditMask);
  };

  it("opens for a mask", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);

    openOptions(mask);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toEqual({ maskId: mask.id, mode: "editing" });
  });

  it("turns clipping off and on without losing the masked element", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);
    const before = [content(mask), content(target)];
    openOptions(mask);

    API.executeAction(actionToggleMaskEnabled);
    expect(API.getElement(mask).maskEnabled).toBe(false);
    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);

    API.executeAction(actionToggleMaskEnabled);
    expect(API.getElement(mask).maskEnabled).toBe(true);

    expect([content(mask), content(target)]).toEqual(before);
  });

  it("can undo turning clipping off", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);
    openOptions(mask);
    API.executeAction(actionToggleMaskEnabled);

    Keyboard.undo();

    expect(API.getElement(mask).maskEnabled).toBe(true);
  });

  it("removes the mask and closes", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    createMask(mask, target);
    openOptions(mask);

    API.executeAction(actionRemoveMask);

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(null);
    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-22 02:02:27Z)**_

There's no proper UI yet. The button is step 4, and double-click picking is step 3. But in `yarn start` dev mode the editor exposes `window.h` to the browser console, so you can trigger the double-click step by hand and see the step 1 and step 2 work for real.

**Setup**

1. Run `yarn start` and open the app.
2. Draw an **ellipse**, then a **rectangle** with a fill colour that overlaps it.
3. Open the browser console with F12.

**Create a mask**

1. Select only the ellipse and press **Ctrl+Alt+G**. You won't see anything happen: masking mode is on, but its bar comes in step 3. While it's on, most keys are blocked; that's the partial step 3 code.
2. Paste this into the console. It does what double-clicking the rectangle will do once step 3 exists:
   ```js
   h.app.actionManager.executeAction(
     h.app.actionManager.actions.applyMask,
     "api",
     h.elements.find((e) => e.type === "rectangle").id,
   );
   ```

**What you should see**

- **Clipping:** the rectangle only shows inside the ellipse.
- **Preview:** the ellipse ends up selected, so the hidden part of the rectangle shows at 20% opacity. Click empty canvas to deselect and the hidden part disappears.
- **Moving the mask:** drag the ellipse, and a different part of the rectangle shows while the rectangle stays put. Rotate and resize it too.
- **Rounded shapes:** repeat with a diamond, triangle or rounded rectangle as the mask.
- **Turning clipping off and on:** select the ellipse, then paste:
  ```js
  const am = h.app.actionManager;
  am.executeAction(am.actions.editMask);
  am.executeAction(am.actions.toggleMaskEnabled);
  ```
  The whole rectangle reappears. Run it again and it's clipped again.
- **Removing:** select the ellipse and press Ctrl+Alt+G. The rectangle is whole again.
- **Releasing:** while it's masked, select only the rectangle and press Ctrl+Alt+G. The rectangle is released.
- **Undo and redo:** Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y step through each of the above.
- **Export:** with the mask applied, open Export image (Ctrl+Shift+E) and save a PNG and an SVG. Both should show the clip, and neither should include the 20% preview.
- **Ctrl+G** on two shapes still groups them.

One caveat: if you press Ctrl+Alt+G and _don't_ apply a mask, press Escape to leave masking mode. Until then, keyboard shortcuts stay blocked.

+  private handleMaskEditorKeyDown = (

## Step 3: Masking mode, in detail

**Goal:** after Ctrl+Alt+G on a basic shape, the user double-clicks one element to mask it. Only panning and zooming work until they pick something or cancel.

**3a. Finish the input blocking in `App.tsx`**

- Keyboard: already written, kept as is.
- Pointer: already written. Clicks and drags on the canvas do nothing, while panning with Space-drag, the middle mouse button or the hand tool still works, and so does wheel zoom.
- Leave masking mode if the parent shape is deleted (for example by undo) or the active tool changes. That's a small check in `componentDidUpdate`.

**3b. Double-click handling in `handleCanvasDoubleClick`**, checked before anything else:

- on an element that can be masked → `applyMask`, which clips it, selects the mask and leaves the mode;
- on empty canvas → `cancelMasking`;
- on an element that can't be masked (the shape itself, another mask, something already masked, an image, a frame, an embed) → ignored, and the mode stays on;
- in masking mode, double-clicking never opens a text box.

**3c. The `MaskingModeBar` component**, in a new `MaskingModeBar.tsx` plus `.scss`:

- fixed at the bottom centre of the screen, in the same Island style as the top toolbar;
- text: "Double-click an element to mask it", which is already in `en.json`;
- a **Cancel** button in the Excalidraw+ grey, light and dark. That button's colours live in the app's `.plus-banner` styles, so I'll copy the values into the package's own `.scss` rather than import from the app;
- it renders only while `maskEditor.mode === "picking"`.

**3d. Tests**, added to `maskActions.test.tsx` or a new `maskingMode.test.tsx`:

- double-clicking an eligible element applies the mask; empty canvas cancels; an ineligible element is ignored;
- clicking or dragging during the mode doesn't change the selection or move anything;
- Escape and Ctrl+Alt+G cancel; zoom shortcuts still work; other shortcuts (for example R for rectangle) are blocked;
- the bar shows during the mode, its Cancel button works, and it's hidden otherwise;
- deleting the parent ends the mode.

**How you check it:** the typecheck and tests, then `yarn start`:

- select an ellipse, press Ctrl+Alt+G, see the bar, double-click a rectangle, and it's clipped;
- try Cancel, Escape, double-clicking empty canvas, and panning and zooming while picking;
- check the bar in light and dark mode.
