import clsx from "clsx";

import { actionShortcuts } from "../../actions";
import { useTunnels } from "../../context/tunnels";
import { ExitZenModeButton, UndoRedoActions, ZoomActions } from "../Actions";
import { HelpButton } from "../HelpButton";
import { Section } from "../Section";
import Stack from "../Stack";

import type { ActionManager } from "../../actions/manager";
import type { UIAppState } from "../../types";

const Footer = ({
  appState,
  actionManager,
  showExitZenModeBtn,
  renderWelcomeScreen,
}: {
  appState: UIAppState;
  actionManager: ActionManager;
  showExitZenModeBtn: boolean;
  renderWelcomeScreen: boolean;
}) => {
  const { FooterCenterTunnel, WelcomeScreenHelpHintTunnel } = useTunnels();

  return (
    <footer
      role="contentinfo"
      className="layer-ui__wrapper__footer App-menu App-menu_bottom"
    >
      <div
        className={clsx("layer-ui__wrapper__footer-left zen-mode-transition", {
          "layer-ui__wrapper__footer-left--transition-left":
            appState.zenModeEnabled,
        })}
      >
        <Stack.Col gap={2}>
          <Section heading="canvasActions">
            <ZoomActions renderAction={actionManager.renderAction} />

            {!appState.viewModeEnabled && (
              <UndoRedoActions
                renderAction={actionManager.renderAction}
                className={clsx("zen-mode-transition", {
                  "layer-ui__wrapper__footer-left--transition-bottom":
                    appState.zenModeEnabled,
                })}
              />
            )}
          </Section>
        </Stack.Col>
      </div>
      <FooterCenterTunnel.Out />
      <div
        className={clsx("layer-ui__wrapper__footer-right zen-mode-transition", {
          "transition-right": appState.zenModeEnabled,
        })}
      >
        <div style={{ position: "relative" }}>
          {renderWelcomeScreen && <WelcomeScreenHelpHintTunnel.Out />}
          <HelpButton
            onClick={() => actionManager.executeAction(actionShortcuts)}
          />
        </div>
      </div>
      <ExitZenModeButton
        actionManager={actionManager}
        showExitZenModeBtn={showExitZenModeBtn}
      />
    </footer>
  );
};

export default Footer;
Footer.displayName = "Footer";

import React from "react";
import clsx from "clsx";

import "./Island.scss";

import type { ViewportUIDock, ViewportUIName } from "../types";

type IslandProps = {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  padding?: number;
  className?: string | boolean;
  style?: object;
  /** marks the island as a canvas-occluding UI surface measured by
   * `getViewportOffsets` (see {@link ViewportUIDock}) */
  "data-viewport-ui"?: ViewportUIDock;
  /** identifies the surface so `getViewportOffsets` can reserve space for
   * it while hidden (see {@link ViewportUIName}) */
  "data-viewport-ui-name"?: ViewportUIName;
};

export const Island = React.forwardRef<HTMLDivElement, IslandProps>(
  (
    {
      children,
      padding,
      className,
      style,
      "data-viewport-ui": viewportUI,
      "data-viewport-ui-name": viewportUIName,
    },
    ref,
  ) => (
    <div
      className={clsx("Island", className)}
      style={{ "--padding": padding, ...style }}
      data-viewport-ui={viewportUI}
      data-viewport-ui-name={viewportUIName}
      ref={ref}
    >
      {children}
    </div>
  ),
);

```typescript
import React from "react";

import { CODES, KEYS } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { CaptureUpdateAction } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { NonDeletedExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Keyboard, Pointer } from "./helpers/ui";
import {
  act,
  fireEvent,
  GlobalTestState,
  render,
  screen,
  unmountComponent,
} from "./test-utils";

const { h } = window;

const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");

const MASKING_HINT = "Double-click an element to mask it";

const pressMaskShortcut = () => {
  fireEvent.keyDown(document, {
    key: KEYS.G,
    code: CODES.G,
    ctrlKey: true,
    altKey: true,
  });
};

/**
 * mask: filled ellipse at (0, 0)–(100, 100)
 * target: filled rectangle at (200, 0)–(300, 100)
 */
const setup = () => {
  const mask = API.createElement({
    type: "ellipse",
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    width: 100,
    height: 100,
    backgroundColor: "#a5d8ff",
    fillStyle: "solid",
  });
  const target = API.createElement({
    type: "rectangle",
    x: 200,
    y: 0,
    width: 100,
    height: 100,
    backgroundColor: "#ffc9c9",
    fillStyle: "solid",
  });
  API.updateScene({
    elements: [mask, target],
    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
  });
  return { mask, target };
};

/** sets up the scene and enters masking mode with the ellipse as the mask */
const startMasking = () => {
  const elements = setup();
  API.setSelectedElements([elements.mask]);
  pressMaskShortcut();
  expect(h.state.maskEditor?.mode).toBe("picking");
  return elements;
};

beforeEach(async () => {
  unmountComponent();
  mouse.reset();
  await render(<Excalidraw autoFocus={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
  Object.assign(document, {
    elementFromPoint: () => GlobalTestState.canvas,
  });
});

describe("picking the element to mask", () => {
  it("masks the double-clicked element", () => {
    const { mask, target } = startMasking();

    mouse.doubleClickAt(250, 50);

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);
    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [mask.id]: true });
  });

  it("doesn't open a text editor on the picked element", () => {
    startMasking();

    mouse.doubleClickAt(250, 50);

    expect(h.state.editingTextElement).toBe(null);
  });

  it("cancels when double-clicking empty canvas", () => {
    const { target } = startMasking();

    mouse.doubleClickAt(600, 600);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBeUndefined();
    expect(h.state.editingTextElement).toBe(null);
  });

  it("ignores the mask itself and stays in masking mode", () => {
    const { mask } = startMasking();

    mouse.doubleClickAt(50, 50);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toEqual({ maskId: mask.id, mode: "picking" });
    expect(API.getElement(mask).maskId).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("ignores elements that can't be masked", () => {
    startMasking();
    const image = API.createElement({
      type: "image",
      x: 400,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
    });
    API.updateScene({
      elements: [...h.elements, image],
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });

    mouse.doubleClickAt(450, 50);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor?.mode).toBe("picking");
    expect(API.getElement(image).maskId).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe("masking mode input", () => {
  it("doesn't select or move elements on click or drag", () => {
    const { mask, target } = startMasking();

    mouse.downAt(250, 50);
    mouse.moveTo(350, 150);
    mouse.upAt(350, 150);

    expect(API.getElement(target).x).toBe(200);
    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [mask.id]: true });
    expect(h.state.maskEditor?.mode).toBe("picking");
  });

  it("blocks other shortcuts", () => {
    startMasking();

    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.R);

    expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("selection");
    expect(h.state.maskEditor?.mode).toBe("picking");
  });

  it("lets zoom shortcuts through", () => {
    startMasking();
    const zoom = h.state.zoom.value;

    fireEvent.keyDown(document, {
      key: "=",
      code: CODES.EQUAL,
      ctrlKey: true,
    });

    expect(h.state.zoom.value).toBeGreaterThan(zoom);
    expect(h.state.maskEditor?.mode).toBe("picking");
  });

  it("cancels on Escape", () => {
    startMasking();

    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });

  it("ends when another tool is picked", () => {
    startMasking();

    act(() => {
      h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "rectangle" });
    });

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });

  it("ends when the mask is deleted", () => {
    const { mask } = startMasking();

    API.updateScene({
      elements: h.elements.map((el) =>
        el.id === mask.id ? { ...el, isDeleted: true } : el,
      ),
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });
});

describe("masking mode bar", () => {
  it("is only shown while picking", () => {
    setup();
    expect(screen.queryByText(MASKING_HINT)).toBe(null);

    API.setSelectedElements([h.elements[0] as NonDeletedExcalidrawElement]);
    pressMaskShortcut();
    expect(screen.queryByText(MASKING_HINT)).not.toBe(null);

    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);
    expect(screen.queryByText(MASKING_HINT)).toBe(null);
  });

  it("cancels masking with its Cancel button", () => {
    const { target } = startMasking();

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("masking-mode-cancel"));

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

Step 3 is code-complete and passes its tests. It still needs your check in the app.

**What changed:**

- **[App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx)**:
  - **Picking:** in masking mode, a double-click goes to the new `handleMaskingModeDoubleClick`.
    - On an element that can be masked, it applies the mask. Double-clicking a shape's text counts as the shape.
    - On empty canvas, it cancels.
    - Elements that can't be masked are ignored, and the mode stays on. Double-clicking never opens a text box during the mode.
  - **Input blocking:** the pointer-down block and the key handling, both from yesterday. Only panning, zooming, Escape and Ctrl+Alt+G work during the mode.
  - **Exiting:** a check in `componentDidUpdate` ends masking mode if another tool is picked, and closes the mask editor if the mask is deleted (for example by undo).
- **New [MaskingModeBar.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/MaskingModeBar.tsx) and [.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/MaskingModeBar.scss)**: the hint "Double-click an element to mask it" plus a Cancel button. The button copies the Excalidraw+ button's styles, including dark mode, using the package's own CSS variables.
- **[LayerUI.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/LayerUI.tsx)**: the bar sits in the existing bottom-centre floating stack, the same spot toasts and "Scroll back to content" use. If a toast appears during the mode, it stacks above the bar instead of overlapping it.

**Checks:**

- **Typecheck:** passes.
- **New [maskingMode.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/maskingMode.test.tsx), 13 tests:** picking, cancelling, ignored elements, no text editor, clicking and dragging blocked, R blocked, zoom allowed, Escape, tool switch, deleted mask, and the bar's visibility and Cancel button. When I removed the step 3 code from a copy of the file, the 4 tests that depend on it failed, so they catch regressions.
- **Other suites:** step 1 and 2 mask tests, context menu, history, regression and grid panel. 240 passed and 1 skipped (that one was already skipped). The text-editor test path I passed doesn't exist, so that suite didn't run.

**Still open:**

- On **phone-sized screens**, the bar doesn't appear, because the phone layout doesn't render that bottom stack. Masking mode still works there, and Escape still cancels. Fine to leave for now, or should I add it?
- The bar sits a little above the footer row rather than flush with the bottom edge, since that's where the existing floating stack lives.

**To check it yourself** in `yarn start`, with no console needed:

1. Draw a filled ellipse and a filled rectangle.
2. Select the ellipse and press Ctrl+Alt+G. The bar appears at the bottom.
3. While picking, try clicking, dragging and pressing R; nothing should happen. Space-drag panning, the scroll wheel and Ctrl+= zoom should still work.
4. Double-click the rectangle. It's clipped, and the bar disappears.
5. Start again and try each way out: Cancel, Escape, double-clicking empty canvas, and picking another tool.
6. Double-click the ellipse itself while picking; nothing should happen.
7. Switch to dark mode and hover over Cancel.

import React from "react";

import { queryByTestId } from "@testing-library/react";

import { CaptureUpdateAction } from "@excalidraw/element";

import { actionApplyMask } from "../actions";
import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { act, fireEvent, render, unmountComponent } from "./test-utils";

const { h } = window;

const openExtraToolsMenu = () => {
  fireEvent.click(
    document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger")!,
  );
  return document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
    ".App-toolbar__extra-tools-dropdown",
  )!;
};

const getMaskItem = () =>
  queryByTestId(openExtraToolsMenu(), "toolbar-mask") as HTMLButtonElement;

const setup = () => {
  const mask = API.createElement({ type: "ellipse" });
  const target = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 50, y: 50 });
  API.updateScene({
    elements: [mask, target],
    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
  });
  return { mask, target };
};

beforeEach(async () => {
  unmountComponent();
  await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
});

describe("Mask item in More tools", () => {
  it("sits directly under the Frame tool", () => {
    const menu = openExtraToolsMenu();
    const frameItem = queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-frame")!;

    expect(frameItem.nextElementSibling).toBe(
      queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-mask"),
    );
  });

  it("shows the shortcut", () => {
    expect(getMaskItem().textContent).toMatch(/Ctrl\+Alt\+G/);
  });

  it("is disabled when nothing it can act on is selected", () => {
    setup();
    expect(getMaskItem().disabled).toBe(true);
  });

  it("enters masking mode for a selected basic shape", () => {
    const { mask } = setup();
    API.setSelectedElements([mask]);

    const item = getMaskItem();
    expect(item.disabled).toBe(false);
    fireEvent.click(item);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toEqual({ maskId: mask.id, mode: "picking" });
  });

  it("removes the mask when a mask is selected", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    API.setSelectedElements([mask]);
    fireEvent.click(getMaskItem());
    act(() => {
      h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionApplyMask, "api", target.id);
    });
    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);

    fireEvent.click(getMaskItem());

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(null);
  });
});

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-22 16:07:11Z)**_

You should fix it yourself rather than leave it to the reviewer. On GitHub, the PR's author resolves conflicts. A PR with a conflict shows "This branch has conflicts that must be resolved" and can't be merged, so the reviewer would either send it back to you or resolve it in GitHub's web editor. In that editor, they couldn't run the tests or snapshot updates afterwards.

Fixing it doesn't cost you a second review, as long as you do it **before you open the PR**. A merge from master is just another commit on your branch. What would cost a second review is resolving it _after_ someone has approved, because new commits can dismiss an approval, depending on your repo's settings.

**When:** after step 5, right before you open the PR. Step 5 touches `App.tsx` again (the double-click dialog), so merging now could leave you resolving twice. It's still one import conflict either way, so doing it now is fine if you'd rather get it out of the way.

**What it involves:**

1. Run `git merge origin/master`.
2. In `App.tsx`, keep both sides of the import list: their `actionToggleCollaboratorVisibility` and our ten mask and zoom imports.
3. Rerun the typecheck and tests, and update the app-state snapshots if they changed.
4. Quick check in the app: masks with a hidden collaborator.
5. Commit the merge, then open the PR.

I can walk through it with you or do it when you're ready.

import React from "react";

import {
  PATH_MOTION_SPEED_PRESETS,
  sceneCoordsToViewportCoords,
} from "@excalidraw/common";
import { getElementAbsoluteCoords } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type {
  ElementsMap,
  ExcalidrawPathElement,
  NonDeleted,
  PathMotionConfig,
  PathMotionEasing,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import {
  actionChangeMotionPathConfig,
  actionFinishMotionPathEdit,
  actionRejectMotionPathEdit,
  actionToggleMotionPathCurve,
} from "../actions";
import { t } from "../i18n";

import { useExcalidrawActionManager, useExcalidrawAppState } from "./App";

import "./MotionPathEditToolbar.scss";

/** clears the path's top-right resize handle */
const HANDLE_CLEARANCE = 24;

/**
 * Small floating toolbar shown next to a motion path while it is being
 * re-edited (see actionMotionPathEditor.tsx). Positioned like
 * ElementCanvasButtons, and hidden under the same conditions plus while the
 * path is being dragged, so it never sits under the pointer mid-gesture.
 */
export const MotionPathEditToolbar = ({
  path,
  elementsMap,
  isPlaying,
  canReset,
  onPlay,
  onPause,
  onReset,
}: {
  path: NonDeleted<ExcalidrawPathElement>;
  elementsMap: ElementsMap;
  isPlaying: boolean;
  canReset: boolean;
  onPlay: () => void;
  onPause: () => void;
  onReset: () => void;
}) => {
  const appState = useExcalidrawAppState();
  const actionManager = useExcalidrawActionManager();

  if (
    appState.contextMenu ||
    appState.newElement ||
    appState.resizingElement ||
    appState.isRotating ||
    appState.openMenu ||
    appState.viewModeEnabled ||
    appState.selectedElementsAreBeingDragged ||
    appState.selectedLinearElement?.isDragging
  ) {
    return null;
  }

  const [, y1, x2] = getElementAbsoluteCoords(path, elementsMap);
  const { x: viewportX, y: viewportY } = sceneCoordsToViewportCoords(
    { sceneX: x2, sceneY: y1 },
    appState,
  );

  return (
    <div
      className="motion-path-edit-toolbar"
      data-testid="motion-path-edit-toolbar"
      style={{
        top: `${viewportY - appState.offsetTop}px`,
        left: `${viewportX - appState.offsetLeft + HANDLE_CLEARANCE}px`,
      }}
    >
      <div className="motion-path-edit-toolbar__row">
        <button
          type="button"
          className="motion-path-edit-toolbar__button motion-path-edit-toolbar__button--primary"
          data-testid={isPlaying ? "motion-path-pause" : "motion-path-play"}
          onClick={isPlaying ? onPause : onPlay}
        >
          {isPlaying
            ? t("labels.pathEditor.pause")
            : t("labels.pathEditor.play")}
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="motion-path-edit-toolbar__button"
          data-testid="motion-path-reset"
          disabled={!canReset}
          onClick={onReset}
        >
          {t("labels.pathEditor.reset")}
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="motion-path-edit-toolbar__button"
          data-testid="motion-path-curve"
          aria-pressed={!!path.roundness}
          onClick={() =>
            actionManager.executeAction(actionToggleMotionPathCurve)
          }
        >
          {path.roundness
            ? t("labels.pathEditor.straight")
            : t("labels.pathEditor.curved")}
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="motion-path-edit-toolbar__button"
          data-testid="motion-path-reject"
          onClick={() =>

          }
        >
          {t("labels.pathEditor.reject")}
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="motion-path-edit-toolbar__button"
          data-testid="motion-path-done"
          onClick={() =>
            actionManager.executeAction(actionFinishMotionPathEdit)
          }
        >
          {t("labels.pathEditor.done")}
        </button>
      </div>
      <MotionSettings

import clsx from "clsx";

import "./Switch.scss";

export type SwitchProps = {
  name: string;
  checked: boolean;
  title?: string;
  onChange: (value: boolean) => void;
  disabled?: boolean;
};

export const Switch = ({
  title,
  name,
  checked,
  onChange,
  disabled = false,
}: SwitchProps) => {
  return (
    <div className={clsx("Switch", { toggled: checked, disabled })}>
      <input
        name={name}
        id={name}
        title={title}
        type="checkbox"
        checked={checked}
        disabled={disabled}
        onChange={() => onChange(!checked)}
        onKeyDown={(event) => {
          if (event.key === " ") {
            onChange(!checked);
          }
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
};

import React from "react";

import { sceneCoordsToViewportCoords } from "@excalidraw/common";
import { getElementAbsoluteCoords, isMaskEnabled } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type {
  ElementsMap,
  NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { actionRemoveMask, actionToggleMaskEnabled } from "../actions";
import { t } from "../i18n";

import { useExcalidrawActionManager, useExcalidrawAppState } from "./App";
import { Switch } from "./Switch";

import "./MaskEditToolbar.scss";

/** clears the mask's top-right resize handle */
const HANDLE_CLEARANCE = 24;

/**
 * Mask options, shown next to a mask shape after double-clicking it (see
 * actionMask.tsx). Positioned and hidden like MotionPathEditToolbar.
 */
export const MaskEditToolbar = ({
  mask,
  elementsMap,
}: {
  mask: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement;
  elementsMap: ElementsMap;
}) => {
  const appState = useExcalidrawAppState();
  const actionManager = useExcalidrawActionManager();

  if (
    appState.contextMenu ||
    appState.newElement ||
    appState.resizingElement ||
    appState.isRotating ||
    appState.openMenu ||
    appState.viewModeEnabled ||
    appState.selectedElementsAreBeingDragged
  ) {
    return null;
  }

  const [, y1, x2] = getElementAbsoluteCoords(mask, elementsMap);
  const { x: viewportX, y: viewportY } = sceneCoordsToViewportCoords(
    { sceneX: x2, sceneY: y1 },
    appState,
  );

  return (
    <div
      className="mask-edit-toolbar"
      data-testid="mask-edit-toolbar"
      style={{
        top: `${viewportY - appState.offsetTop}px`,
        left: `${viewportX - appState.offsetLeft + HANDLE_CLEARANCE}px`,
      }}
    >
      <label className="mask-edit-toolbar__toggle">
        <span>{t("labels.mask.enabled")}</span>
        <Switch
          name="mask-enabled"
          checked={isMaskEnabled(mask)}
          onChange={() => actionManager.executeAction(actionToggleMaskEnabled)}
        />
      </label>
      <button
        type="button"
        className="mask-edit-toolbar__button"
        data-testid="mask-remove"
        onClick={() => actionManager.executeAction(actionRemoveMask)}
      >
        {t("labels.mask.remove")}
      </button>
    </div>
  );
};
```

import React from "react";

import { CODES, KEYS } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { CaptureUpdateAction } from "@excalidraw/element";

import { actionApplyMask } from "../actions";
import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Keyboard, Pointer } from "./helpers/ui";
import {
  act,
  fireEvent,
  GlobalTestState,
  render,
  screen,
  unmountComponent,
} from "./test-utils";

const { h } = window;

const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");

const getTextarea = () =>
  document.querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>(
    ".excalidraw-textEditorContainer > textarea",
  );

const getToolbar = () => screen.queryByTestId("mask-edit-toolbar");

/**
 * mask: filled ellipse at (0, 0)–(100, 100), clipping
 * target: filled rectangle at (50, 50)–(150, 150)
 */
const setupMask = () => {
  const mask = API.createElement({
    type: "ellipse",
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    width: 100,
    height: 100,
    backgroundColor: "#a5d8ff",
    fillStyle: "solid",
  });
  const target = API.createElement({
    type: "rectangle",
    x: 50,
    y: 50,
    width: 100,
    height: 100,
    backgroundColor: "#ffc9c9",
    fillStyle: "solid",
  });
  API.updateScene({
    elements: [mask, target],
    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
  });
  API.setSelectedElements([mask]);
  fireEvent.keyDown(document, {
    key: KEYS.G,
    code: CODES.G,
    ctrlKey: true,
    altKey: true,
  });
  act(() => {
    h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionApplyMask, "api", target.id);
  });
  expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);
  return { mask, target };
};

/** double-click the mask, close its text editor, double-click it again */
const openOptions = () => {
  mouse.doubleClickAt(20, 50);
  const textarea = getTextarea();
  expect(textarea).not.toBe(null);
  Keyboard.exitTextEditor(textarea!);
  mouse.doubleClickAt(20, 50);
};

beforeEach(async () => {
  unmountComponent();
  mouse.reset();
  await render(<Excalidraw autoFocus={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
  Object.assign(document, {
    elementFromPoint: () => GlobalTestState.canvas,
  });
});

describe("opening the mask options", () => {
  it("edits the mask's text on the first double-click", () => {
    setupMask();

    mouse.doubleClickAt(20, 50);

    expect(getTextarea()).not.toBe(null);
    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });

  it("opens the options on the next double-click", () => {
    const { mask } = setupMask();

    openOptions();

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toEqual({ maskId: mask.id, mode: "editing" });
    expect(getToolbar()).not.toBe(null);
    expect(getTextarea()).toBe(null);
  });

  it("keeps double-click inside the text box for selecting words", () => {
    setupMask();
    mouse.doubleClickAt(20, 50);
    const textarea = getTextarea()!;

    fireEvent.doubleClick(textarea);

    expect(getTextarea()).toBe(textarea);
    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });

  it("never opens for shapes that aren't masks", () => {
    setupMask();
    const shape = API.createElement({
      type: "rectangle",
      x: 300,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
      backgroundColor: "#b2f2bb",
      fillStyle: "solid",
    });
    API.updateScene({
      elements: [...h.elements, shape],
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });

    mouse.doubleClickAt(350, 50);
    Keyboard.exitTextEditor(getTextarea()!);
    mouse.doubleClickAt(350, 50);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect(getTextarea()).not.toBe(null);
  });
});

describe("mask options", () => {
  it("turns clipping off and on with the switch", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setupMask();
    openOptions();
    const toggle = () =>
      fireEvent.click(
        document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[name="mask-enabled"]')!,
      );

    toggle();
    expect(API.getElement(mask).maskEnabled).toBe(false);
    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(mask.id);

    toggle();
    expect(API.getElement(mask).maskEnabled).toBe(true);
  });

  it("removes the mask and closes", () => {
    const { target } = setupMask();
    openOptions();

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("mask-remove"));

    expect(API.getElement(target).maskId).toBe(null);
    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect(getToolbar()).toBe(null);
  });

  it("closes on Escape", () => {
    setupMask();
    openOptions();

    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
    expect(getToolbar()).toBe(null);
  });

  it("closes when the mask is deselected", () => {
    setupMask();
    openOptions();

    API.setSelectedElements([]);

    expect(h.state.maskEditor).toBe(null);
  });
});

Step 5 is code-complete and passes its tests. I see you've committed step 4 (`f92f1b4f`) and reworded step 3 to "manual mask".

**What changed:**

- **New [MaskEditToolbar.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/MaskEditToolbar.tsx) and [.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/MaskEditToolbar.scss)**: a small floating panel at the mask's top-right corner, positioned and styled like the motion path toolbar.
  - **Clipping switch:** uses the existing `Switch` component and turns clipping off and on.
  - **"Remove mask" button:** removes the mask and closes the panel.
  - The panel hides while you drag, resize or rotate, or while a menu is open.
- **[App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx)**:
  - **Double-clicking a mask:**
    - the first double-click edits its text as usual;
    - the next double-click on the same mask opens the options instead;
    - double-clicking anything else resets this.
    - The transparent inside of a selected mask counts as the mask.
    - A double-click inside the text box never reaches the canvas, so it still selects words.
  - **Closing:** the panel closes on Escape (from step 3), when the mask is deselected, or when it's removed or deleted.
- **[actionMask.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionMask.tsx)**: `editMask` can open the options for a given mask, and selects it when it does.

**Checks:**

- **Typecheck:** passes.
- **New [maskEditor.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/maskEditor.test.tsx), 8 tests:**
  - the first double-click edits text; the next opens the options;
  - a double-click inside the text box keeps the text editor;
  - shapes that aren't masks never get the options;
  - the switch turns clipping off and on;
  - Remove works;
  - Escape and deselecting both close the panel.
- **Tests that can fail:** when I disabled the dialog trigger, 3 tests failed and 2 still passed, which exposed a weakness in those 2. I tightened them so they now require the dialog to have opened first.
- **All 5 mask test files plus the large suites:** context menu, history, regression, grid panel, and this time the text-editor suite too. 333 passed and 2 skipped (both were already skipped).

**One behaviour to judge in the app:** the "next double-click opens the options" rule doesn't expire. If you double-click a mask to edit its text and come back much later, the next double-click on it opens the options, not the text editor, unless you double-clicked something else in between. It matches what you described; say if you'd rather it reset when the mask is deselected.

**To check it yourself** in `yarn start`:

1. Mask a rectangle with an ellipse.
2. Double-click the ellipse and a text box opens. Type something, then click away or press Escape.
3. Double-click the ellipse again and the options panel appears.
4. Toggle Clipping off and on, and watch the rectangle.
5. Press Escape and the panel closes. Reopen it, then click empty canvas, and it closes.
6. Reopen it and click "Remove mask".
7. While the text box is open, double-click a word inside it. It should select the word, not open the panel.
8. Repeat in dark mode.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-22 16:48:20Z)**_

It's not strictly required, but the conflict has to be resolved somewhere before the PR can be merged, and those 49 files won't show up as your changes in the PR.

GitHub compares your branch against master, and those 49 files are master's own changes (mostly #116's). After the merge they're identical on both sides, so the PR's "Files changed" tab still shows only your mask work plus the one import-list line. The merge just appears as one extra commit, "Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master'…", in the PR's commit list.

Your options:

1. **Commit the merge (recommended).** It's already resolved and tested, so this is the least work, and the PR opens with no conflict. The cost is one merge commit in your branch's history.
2. **Rebase instead of merging.** Undo with `git merge --abort`, then run `git rebase origin/master`. Your 5 commits are replayed on top of master, so the history stays linear with no merge commit. The import conflict comes up again while replaying the step 3 commit, and I'd resolve it the same way. Because your commits aren't pushed yet, the push is still a normal fast-forward with no force-push. It's slightly more work but gives the tidiest history.
3. **Don't sync at all.** Run `git merge --abort` and open the PR as is. GitHub then shows "This branch has conflicts," and someone has to resolve it in the web editor, with no chance to run the tests. That's what you wanted to avoid.

If your team doesn't care about merge commits (your master history is all PR merge commits anyway), go with option 1. If you'd prefer a clean history, I can switch to option 2.
